reasoning:
**What is asked.** The 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED series DGS10) for Friday 4 December 2026, in percent, as first published.

**Starting point.** The yield ended Tuesday 17 November 2026 near 5.10% and traded about 5.09% early on 18 November (Trading Economics). It was 5.13% on Monday 16 November (TheStreet Pro, Trading Economics) and 5.16% on Friday 13 November, its highest since October. Over the past four weeks it is down about 3 basis points, so it has been moving inside a band of roughly 4.9% to 5.2%.

**Time left.** Twelve trading days (Thanksgiving closed, 27 November shortened). Daily moves of 6 to 7 basis points are normal at this level and in this climate, which gives a standard deviation of about 23 basis points by 4 December.

**What is scheduled.** FOMC minutes on 18 November; PCE inflation and Treasury auctions in Thanksgiving week; ISM surveys in the first days of December; and the November jobs report, due on the morning of 4 December itself, so the resolving value should include that day's reaction. The Fed meets on 8-9 December, after the period. Futures put a quarter-point hike at about 95% (CME FedWatch, 16 November), so the decision is largely in the price. The risks run both ways: hot October inflation and oil keep pressure upward, while the selloff in AI shares could still bring a safe-haven bid, which it has not done so far.

**Forecast.** I centre on the latest value with no drift and keep the tails wide: median 5.10%, middle half 4.96% to 5.24%, 5th to 95th percentile 4.72% to 5.47%. A close under 4.7% would need a growth scare or a sharp flight to safety. One above 5.5% would need a strong jobs report on top of another inflation surprise.
